description: Canonical evidence reasoning behavior for A.R.I.A. The Evidence Engine interprets, normalizes, verifies, relates, and evaluates canonical evidence while preserving provenance, dependency, contradiction, uncertainty, and historical traceability. Evidence vocabulary is owned by the Evidence Types Registry and persisted evidence structure is owned by the Evidence Schema.

core_principle.statement: Evidence is a traceable observation or information-bearing technical record relevant to reasoning. Evidence is not automatically fact, interpretation is not observation, correlation is not causation, and A.R.I.A.'s own inference does not become independent evidence merely because A.R.I.A. generated it.
rules: Persisted evidence shall conform to Core/Schemas/evidence.schema.json.
Evidence classification shall use Core/Registries/evidence_types.json.
Evidence shall preserve provenance.
Observation shall remain distinguishable from interpretation.
Evidence may be valid while supporting, weakening, or contradicting different hypotheses.
Evidence persistence status shall not encode diagnostic support or confidence.
Evidence shall not establish causality merely because it correlates with an observed condition.
Derived evidence shall remain traceable to its parent evidence and required source values.
Duplicate representations of the same underlying observation shall not become independent corroboration.
Contradictory evidence shall remain visible.
Historical experience is not current-case evidence.
A.R.I.A.-generated interpretation shall not self-validate.
Missing evidence shall not be represented as observed evidence.
Evidence uncertainty shall remain explicit.
The Evidence Engine shall remain technically domain-independent.
Evidence Engine shall not create an alternate evidence identity model.
Canonical sources, artifacts, measurements, contexts, hypotheses, actions, and events shall be referenced when canonical identity exists.
Multiple records derived from the same underlying observation shall preserve dependency relationships.
Evidence identity shall not be duplicated solely because the same observation is represented in multiple formats.
Evidence Engine shall consume evidence_type from the canonical Evidence Types Registry.
Evidence Engine shall not maintain a competing evidence-type list.
Evidence type describes what kind of evidence the record represents and does not establish truth, confidence, independence, or causal significance.
New evidence classifications shall be introduced through the Registry rather than embedded in Evidence Engine logic.
Evidence Engine shall not define a competing evidence_record structure.
Persisted evidence status shall conform to evidence.schema.json.
ACTIVE does not mean proven or supportive.
SUPERSEDED means a more applicable representation has replaced the evidence for current reasoning without erasing history.
INVALIDATED means the evidence has been determined unsuitable as valid evidence.
RETRACTED means the originating authority or responsible process withdrew the evidence.
Contradiction shall not be encoded as persistence status.
Confidence shall not be encoded as persistence status.
Diagnostic effect shall not be encoded as persistence status.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: IDENTIFY_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Identify an observation, measurement, report, artifact, configuration state, system output, or other information-bearing item that may warrant canonical Evidence representation.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: PRESERVE_RAW_OBSERVATION
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Preserve the original observation, artifact, value, statement, or source representation before interpretation.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: CLASSIFY_EVIDENCE
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Assign the applicable canonical evidence_type from the Evidence Types Registry.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: RESOLVE_PROVENANCE
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Resolve source, artifact, measurement, action, event, context, and other provenance references where available.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: NORMALIZE_OBSERVATION
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Normalize representation, units, formatting, timestamps, identifiers, or terminology without altering technical meaning.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: ASSESS_VERIFICATION
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Determine what aspects of the evidence have been verified and what remain reported, inferred, ambiguous, or unverified.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: ASSESS_CONTEXT_APPLICABILITY
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Determine whether the evidence is applicable to the technical subject and reasoning operation under the relevant context.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: ASSESS_QUALITY
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Evaluate relevant quality factors without creating a competing confidence vocabulary.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: ASSESS_DEPENDENCY
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Determine whether the evidence is independent, derived, duplicated, correlated through a common source, or otherwise dependent on other evidence.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: ASSESS_RELATIONSHIPS
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Identify corroboration, contradiction, supersession, invalidation, derivation, or other diagnostically relevant evidence relationships.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: ASSESS_DIAGNOSTIC_EFFECT
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Describe how the evidence may affect applicable hypotheses without directly calculating hypothesis probability.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: IDENTIFY_EVIDENCE_GAPS
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Identify missing observations whose acquisition could materially discriminate important technical possibilities.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: PROPOSE_EVIDENCE_PERSISTENCE
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Create, update, supersede, invalidate, or retract canonical evd_<UUID> state when warranted.

evidence_processing_pipeline.name: RETURN_EVIDENCE_RESULT
evidence_processing_pipeline.description: Return evidence state, quality, relationships, contradictions, gaps, and material changes to Orchestration.

observation_interpretation_boundary.principle: What was observed and what A.R.I.A. believes the observation means shall remain distinguishable.
rules: Raw observations shall be preserved whenever practical.
Normalization shall not silently add interpretation.
Interpretation shall remain attributable to the evidence from which it was derived.
A screenshot showing a value is evidence of what was displayed, not automatically proof that the underlying physical state matched the display.
A user statement is evidence of what the user reported and may also describe a technical observation when appropriately represented.
A diagnostic conclusion derived from evidence is not itself independent evidence.
Interpretation may change as context changes while the original observation remains historically stable.

provenance.principle: Evidence strength and meaning depend on where the evidence came from and how it was produced.
rules: Evidence without complete provenance may still be useful when limitations are preserved.
Unknown provenance shall not be silently converted into trusted provenance.
Evidence derived from another evidence item shall preserve parent references.
A copied artifact shall not automatically become independent evidence.
Evidence provenance shall remain available after supersession or invalidation.

normalization.principle: Normalization improves comparability while preserving the original technical observation.
rules: Raw and normalized values shall remain distinguishable when both are material.
Unit conversion shall preserve the original unit and canonical measurement relationship when applicable.
Normalization shall not increase evidence certainty.
Ambiguous values shall remain ambiguous.
Normalization shall not manufacture missing precision.

verification_reasoning.principle: Verification describes what has been checked about an evidence item without turning verification into a second persistence-status system.
rules: Verification shall use the verification structure provided by evidence.schema.json.
An unverified evidence item may remain ACTIVE.
Verified provenance does not prove the technical interpretation.
Independent reproduction may strengthen confidence but does not automatically establish cause.
Verification limitations shall remain explicit.

quality_assessment.principle: Evidence quality is multidimensional and shall feed the shared confidence architecture without creating a second confidence contract.
rules: Not every quality factor applies to every evidence type.
Evidence Engine shall not require all factors to be scored.
Quality assessment shall not imply false numerical precision.
Applicable shared confidence levels and structures shall be used where confidence is persisted.
Evidence type alone shall not determine confidence.
Direct evidence may still be poor quality.
Indirect evidence may still be useful when its limitations are understood.
High-quality evidence may still be irrelevant if context does not match.

freshness.principle: Evidence applicability may change as the technical system changes.
rules: Old evidence is not automatically invalid.
Recent evidence is not automatically superior.
Freshness matters when the represented technical property could have changed.
Historical evidence shall remain available for historical reconstruction.
Evidence collected before a material context change may require reduced current applicability rather than invalidation.

independence_and_dependency.principle: Multiple evidence records increase corroboration only to the extent they represent genuinely independent information.
rules: Two screenshots of the same underlying display are not automatically independent.
A calculated value derived from a measurement is dependent on that measurement.
A summary generated from an artifact is dependent on the artifact.
Two people repeating information from the same original source are not fully independent.
Independent observations may provide stronger corroboration than dependent observations.
Partially dependent evidence may provide limited additional support.
Unknown dependency shall be treated conservatively.
Dependency affects corroborative weight but does not automatically invalidate the evidence.

duplicate_detection.principle: Duplicate representations shall not create artificial evidence volume.
consider: same user report copied across channels
same log line represented in multiple extracts
same screenshot embedded in multiple documents
derived summaries of the same underlying observation
rules: Duplicate evidence may remain separately persisted when operationally necessary.
Duplicate evidence shall not receive independent corroborative weight.
Duplicate detection shall preserve traceability to all representations.
Similarity alone shall not prove duplication when independent observations could legitimately agree.

derived_evidence.principle: Derived evidence may be diagnostically valuable but shall remain traceable to all evidence required to reproduce the derivation.
rules: Derived evidence shall reference its parent evidence.
Derived evidence shall preserve the derivation method when material.
Derived evidence shall not be treated as independent corroboration of its own parents.
If a required parent is invalidated, dependent derived evidence shall be reevaluated.
Derived evidence may combine multiple independent parents without becoming independent of those parents.
A.R.I.A.'s narrative summary of evidence is not automatically a new evidence item.

negative_evidence.principle: The absence of an expected observation can be evidence when the observation would reasonably have been expected under the relevant conditions.
rules: Failure to observe something is not automatically evidence of absence.
Negative evidence requires an expectation that the condition would have been observable.
Observation method sensitivity and coverage shall be considered.
Negative evidence shall preserve the conditions under which the absence was observed.
Negative evidence may weaken a hypothesis without proving an alternative.

corroboration.principle: Corroboration increases support only when evidence items provide materially distinct information.
rules: Evidence count alone shall not determine corroboration.
Dependent evidence shall receive reduced additional weight.
Independent evidence agreeing on a material technical property may strengthen confidence.
Corroboration does not automatically establish causality.
Corroboration relationships shall remain explainable.

contradiction_handling.principle: Contradictory evidence shall be preserved and investigated rather than silently discarded.
rules: Contradiction is not a persistence status.
Two evidence items may conflict because the technical system changed between observations.
Context differences may explain apparent contradiction.
Measurement error may explain contradiction but shall not be assumed without support.
The evidence favoring the leading hypothesis shall not automatically win.
Unresolved contradiction shall remain visible to Hypothesis, Probability, Uncertainty, Decision, and Validation through Orchestration.
Contradictory evidence shall not be deleted.

diagnostic_effect.principle: Evidence may affect hypotheses in different ways without Evidence Engine owning hypothesis probability.
rules: Diagnostic effect shall be evaluated relative to a specific hypothesis or technical question.
The same evidence may support one hypothesis and contradict another.
Evidence may weaken multiple competing hypotheses simultaneously.
Evidence Engine shall explain the technical basis of the effect.
Probability Engine remains authoritative for probability updates.
Evidence Engine shall not convert effect classes directly into fixed probability changes.
Relationship classes describe Evidence reasoning and shall not replace canonical relationship identity when a persisted relationship object is required.
Relationships shall remain directional when direction is technically meaningful.
SUPERSEDES is distinct from INVALIDATES.
CONTRADICTS is distinct from INVALIDATES.
DERIVED_FROM implies dependency.
DUPLICATES implies no independent corroborative weight.

supersession.principle: Supersession preserves history while identifying evidence that more appropriately represents the applicable current technical state.
rules: Superseded evidence shall remain in case history.
New evidence shall supersede older evidence only when they represent sufficiently comparable technical properties and the newer evidence more appropriately represents the applicable state.
Supersession is not invalidation.
Supersession shall preserve supersedes_evidence_ids and superseded_by_evidence_id according to the Evidence Schema.
Historical reasoning shall remain reconstructable using the evidence available at the time.
A newer observation shall not automatically supersede an older observation when both remain relevant to a changing or intermittent condition.

invalidation.principle: Invalidation means an evidence item is no longer suitable to serve as valid evidence for the represented observation or interpretation.
rules: Contradiction alone does not invalidate evidence.
Age alone does not invalidate evidence.
Low confidence alone does not invalidate evidence.
Invalidated evidence shall remain historically traceable.
Dependent evidence shall be reevaluated when a parent is invalidated.
Invalidation reason shall remain explainable.

retraction.principle: Retraction preserves that an evidence item was withdrawn without erasing its historical role.
rules: Retraction shall use the canonical RETRACTED persistence status.
Retraction shall preserve provenance and prior historical use.
Retraction is distinct from supersession.
Retraction is distinct from invalidation.
Downstream reasoning materially dependent on retracted evidence shall be reevaluated through Orchestration.

human_report_processing.principle: Human reports may contain observations, interpretations, diagnoses, chronology, uncertainty, and requested actions that must remain distinguishable.
extract: what the person believes caused the condition
rules: A person's proposed diagnosis shall not be persisted as though it were a direct observation.
Reported technical values shall preserve their reported provenance.
A technically skilled reporter may justify greater source confidence but not automatic truth.
Repeated reports derived from the same original observation shall not become independent evidence.

artifact_processing.principle: Artifacts are evidence-bearing objects whose contents may generate one or more canonical evidence records.
rules: The original artifact shall remain referenced.
Extracted observations shall preserve artifact provenance.
Multiple observations extracted from one artifact may be distinct evidence while remaining source-dependent.
Artifact interpretation shall distinguish visible content from inferred meaning.
Artifact corruption or incompleteness shall be preserved as a limitation.

measurement_processing.principle: Measurements should reference canonical Measurement objects when the measurement architecture provides canonical identity.
rules: Evidence shall not recreate canonical measurement identity.
Measurement value, unit, method, instrument, tolerance, and timestamp should remain available through the applicable canonical measurement structure.
Evidence may interpret a measurement without changing the underlying measured value.
Converted units shall not create independent evidence.
Measurement uncertainty shall remain distinct from diagnostic uncertainty.

evidence_gap_reasoning.principle: Evidence Engine identifies missing evidence that could materially improve discrimination; it does not select the Action used to obtain it.
rules: Do not identify evidence as missing when sufficiently applicable evidence already exists.
Prefer gaps capable of discriminating important competing hypotheses.
A gap may remain unresolved when acquisition burden exceeds diagnostic value.
Evidence Engine shall not choose the collection Action.
Decision Engine determines whether obtaining additional evidence is worth the required Action.
Routing Engine does not own evidence-acquisition utility scoring.
Orchestration coordinates reevaluation after new evidence arrives.

context_boundary.principle: Context determines evidence applicability; Evidence remains responsible for evidence-specific interpretation and quality.
rules: Evidence Engine shall consume canonical ctx_<UUID> context where applicable.
Evidence Engine shall not recreate the Context Engine.
Context mismatch may reduce applicability without invalidating the observation.
Evidence collected under historical context shall preserve that historical applicability.
Material context uncertainty shall remain visible in evidence assessment.

hypothesis_boundary.principle: Evidence informs hypotheses but does not own hypothesis state or probability.
rules: Evidence Engine may describe whether evidence supports, weakens, contradicts, or discriminates hypotheses.
Hypothesis Engine owns hypothesis reasoning semantics.
Probability Engine owns probability updates.
Evidence Engine shall not confirm a hypothesis solely because supporting evidence exists.
Evidence Engine shall not eliminate a hypothesis solely through a fixed evidence-effect rule.

decision_boundary.principle: Evidence identifies information needs; Decision determines which candidate Action should be selected.
rules: Evidence Engine may identify the expected diagnostic value of additional evidence.
Evidence Engine may identify collection constraints known from the evidence requirement.
Decision Engine compares diagnostic value with action cost, burden, risk, service impact, feasibility, and other decision factors.
Evidence Engine shall not select act_<UUID>.
Evidence Engine shall not bypass Decision by directly requesting execution of a collection procedure.

routing_boundary.principle: Routing manages progression around selected Actions and does not own evidence utility.
rules: Evidence Engine shall not create route steps.
Evidence Engine shall not select next hops.
Evidence Engine shall not reroute.
Routing may expose route state relevant to evidence collection.
New evidence may cause Orchestration to determine that route reevaluation is required.

validation_boundary.principle: Validation may use evidence to determine whether required technical outcomes have been demonstrated; Evidence Engine does not own validation semantics.
rules: Validation evidence remains canonical Evidence.
Evidence quality and applicability remain relevant during validation.
Validation Engine determines whether applicable validation criteria are satisfied.
Successful validation does not retroactively make all prior interpretations correct.
Failed validation may generate new evidence and trigger renewed reasoning.

case_state_boundary.principle: Case State projects which evidence is currently material to the case.
rules: Evidence Engine owns evidence reasoning.
Case State owns assembled case projection.
Case State may project active, superseded, invalidated, and material evidence references.
Evidence Engine shall not directly change lifecycle status.
Material evidence change shall be reported to Orchestration for case-state reconciliation.

orchestration_boundary.principle: Evidence Engine returns evidence reasoning results; Orchestration coordinates downstream effects.
rules: Evidence Engine shall not directly invoke every downstream engine.
Material new evidence shall be reported to Orchestration.
Evidence invalidation, retraction, supersession, contradiction, or material reinterpretation shall be reported to Orchestration.
Orchestration determines whether Context, Hypothesis, Probability, Uncertainty, Decision, Routing, Validation, or Case State require reevaluation.
Evidence Engine shall not publish complete Case State.

historical_integrity.principle: Evidence history shall preserve what was available to reasoning at each historical point.
rules: Superseded evidence shall remain historically available.
Invalidated evidence shall remain historically available with invalidation state.
Retracted evidence shall remain historically available with retraction state.
Later evidence shall not rewrite earlier observations.
Later interpretation may supersede an earlier interpretation without altering the original raw observation.
Historical decisions shall remain reconstructable from evidence available at the time.
Outputs shall distinguish persisted state from proposed state.
Outputs shall preserve uncertainty.
Outputs shall not claim hypothesis probability.
Outputs shall not select Actions.
Outputs shall return material changes to Orchestration.

failure_modes.description: Evidence Engine defines a competing evidence-type vocabulary.
Evidence Engine defines a competing persistence record.
Persistence status is used to encode contradiction, confidence, diagnostic support, or workflow state.
failure_modes.prevention: Use only canonical persistence status semantics.

failure_modes.description: Evidence Engine creates a competing mandatory confidence vocabulary or scoring contract.
failure_modes.prevention: Use shared confidence architecture and evidence-specific quality factors.

failure_modes.description: A.R.I.A.'s interpretation is persisted as though directly observed.
A.R.I.A.-generated inference becomes independent evidence supporting itself.
Multiple representations of the same observation are counted as independent evidence.
failure_modes.prevention: Detect duplicate and dependent evidence families.

failure_modes.description: Evidence conflicting with the leading hypothesis is ignored or removed.
Historical evidence is marked invalid merely because newer evidence exists.
Newer evidence is automatically considered more accurate.
failure_modes.prevention: Assess freshness, quality, context, method, and represented state separately.

failure_modes.description: An observation correlated with a condition is treated as causal proof.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep evidence, hypothesis, probability, and validation responsibilities separate.

failure_modes.description: A similar prior case is treated as an observation in the current case.
failure_modes.prevention: Use experience as prior reasoning input, not current-case evidence.

failure_modes.description: Evidence Engine directly chooses how missing evidence will be obtained.
failure_modes.prevention: Return evidence gaps to Decision through Orchestration.

failure_modes.description: Routing is assigned responsibility for deciding whether evidence acquisition is worth its burden.
Evidence Engine hardcodes microwave, RF, optical, vendor, product, customer, or named-user evidence semantics.

invariants.statement: Evidence type vocabulary is owned by Core/Registries/evidence_types.json.
Persisted evidence structure is owned by Core/Schemas/evidence.schema.json.
Canonical evidence uses evd_<UUID> identity.
Observation and interpretation remain distinguishable.
Evidence persistence status does not encode confidence or diagnostic effect.
Evidence does not automatically establish technical truth or causality.
A.R.I.A.-generated interpretation does not become independent evidence merely because A.R.I.A. generated it.
Derived evidence remains traceable to its parents.
Duplicate representations do not receive independent corroborative weight.
Contradictory evidence remains preserved.
Supersession is distinct from invalidation.
Retraction is distinct from supersession and invalidation.
Historical experience is not current-case evidence.
Evidence Engine does not own hypothesis probability.
Evidence Engine does not select competitive Actions.
Evidence Engine does not perform route progression or rerouting.
Evidence gaps describe information needs rather than selected collection Actions.
Material evidence changes are returned to Orchestration for downstream coordination.
Historical evidence state remains reconstructable.
Evidence Engine remains technically domain-independent.

prohibited_behaviors: Defining a second evidence-type Registry inside Evidence Engine.
Defining a competing evidence persistence schema.
Using evidence persistence status to represent contradiction.
Using evidence persistence status to represent confidence.
Using evidence persistence status to represent hypothesis support.
Creating a mandatory Evidence-specific confidence vocabulary that competes with shared confidence contracts.
Treating interpretation as direct observation.
Treating A.R.I.A.'s inference as independent evidence supporting itself.
Treating duplicate artifacts as independent corroboration.
Treating derived evidence as independent of its parents.
Deleting evidence because it contradicts the leading hypothesis.
Invalidating evidence merely because newer evidence exists.
Treating newer evidence as automatically superior.
Treating a user report as automatically verified fact.
Treating a screenshot as proof of an underlying physical condition beyond what the screenshot establishes.
Treating correlation as causality.
Treating historical experience as current-case evidence.
Directly calculating hypothesis probability.
Directly confirming or eliminating hypotheses.
Directly selecting act_<UUID>.
Directly creating route steps.
Directly rerouting.
Assigning evidence-acquisition utility selection to Routing.
Directly changing case lifecycle status.
Directly invoking downstream engines as a substitute for Orchestration.
Rewriting historical evidence using later knowledge.

Hardcoding microwave-specific, RF-specific, optical-specific, vendor-specific, manufacturer-specific, product-specific, protocol-specific, customer-specific, or named-user evidence logic into universal Evidence Engine semantics.
